column3: The Hebrew says “your bone and your flesh”; BSB uses “your own flesh and blood.”
The Hebrew repeats “Hebron” and “David”; BSB omits the second place name and replaces the second personal name with “him.”
The Hebrew says “house”; BSB uses “palace.” It also explicitly names David where BSB uses “he.”
The Hebrew repeats “David”; BSB uses “he” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew repeats “David”; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “him.”
The Hebrew says that they anointed David, using an active verb; BSB says that David had been anointed.
The Hebrew says “Go up”; BSB says “Go.” The Hebrew also explicitly names David in the reply formula.
The Hebrew uses an unnamed plural subject; BSB identifies it as “the Philistines.”
The Hebrew says “Do not go up”; BSB adds “straight.” The Hebrew says to come to them, where BSB says to attack them.
The Hebrew names Geba; BSB names Gibeon.
